title: Carry the reply note in the prompt so it cannot answer Claude's folder-trust dialog
body:
A Claude dispatched with a prompt into a Remote directory it has not trusted yet quits immediately. Found while verifying hooks (commit 7bdfc18, see its body and docs/remote-sessions.md) and hit by the human in normal use: Claude shows its folder-trust dialog (default selection "No, exit"), the at-launch reply note (src/control/tunnel.rs: reply_note, ReplyNote::arm with at_launch) is injected as soon as the Session is Ready, and the note's trailing Enter answers the dialog with its default, so Claude exits and the Remote Session disconnects.
The human has DECIDED the fix (2026-11-23). Build exactly this, no wider:
1. First launch of an agent with a prompt: the reply instructions travel INSIDE the prompt argument (appended after the brief, separated by a blank line), and NOTHING is typed into the pane at launch. This applies to Claude, Codex and Grok alike. The ReplyNote for that connection must count as delivered, so the first chat delivery does not repeat it.
2. Reconnect: unchanged. A reconnect resumes with no prompt (remote::relaunch), and the token is new per connection, so the note still goes out the way it does today. Do not change reconnect behaviour; pin it with a test if one does not already exist.
3. Anything foreman cannot recognise with certainty as "known agent + a prompt argument" falls back to today's typed note. Never guess which argument is the prompt.
4. A shell, an agent opened with no arguments, and an install Session (remote::install_of) are unchanged.
FIRST, before writing the feature, settle how the prompt argument is identified, and STOP AND REPORT (block the card with the finding, commit nothing speculative) if there is no sound answer. Today's agent detection (remote::agent_of, sharing icons::IconKind::from_argv) is a substring scan of the command line; that is too loose to justify rewriting an argument. You need a rule that is exact for the shapes foreman itself documents and dispatches (read both providers' foreman-dispatch skill copies and the kanban dispatch path for the argv shapes actually produced: bare program name first, flags, the brief as the last positional argument) and that refuses everything else: wrappers, a program path that merely contains an agent name, subcommands (for example codex exec, claude -p / --print, resume forms) unless you have verified the prompt position for that shape, and a last argument that is a flag value rather than a prompt. Write the rule as a pure function with a table test of accepted and refused shapes.
Also check and handle:
- The launch builder's limits (src/remote.rs: build, posix_line, the Windows PowerShell line cap and its argument refusals). The appended note makes the argument longer and adds quotes, newlines and a bearer token; the Posix path base64-encodes the line, the Windows paths have refusals. If appending would make the builder refuse a launch that works today, fall back to the typed note for that launch rather than refuse it.
- The note names the Remote port and the token; confirm both are known when the argv is built (the hook settings JSON already carries them at launch). The token then sits in the agent's argv on the Remote, visible in ps to other users there; the hook settings already put it there, so this adds no new exposure, but say so in docs/remote-sessions.md beside the existing token gotcha.
- The note's wording assumes it arrives as a separate typed message ("[foreman] You run on another PC..."). Inside a prompt it must read as an instruction block that follows the brief, not as part of the task. Keep the command text itself identical (one source of truth: reuse reply_note, do not fork the curl spelling).
- Local Sessions and the control-plane wire format are untouched. No new field on any request.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (section: The way back). Add a Results entry with what you ran and saw. Update docs/remote-sessions.md: the existing gotcha about the launch note landing in a password prompt now applies to reconnect and to the fallback only; state why reconnect still types (token per connection, no prompt to carry it). Both providers' foreman-dispatch skill copies say a Remote agent gets the note at launch: keep them true (embedded-skill rebuild rule in foreman-docs-and-writing).
Verify on the real Remote. Test Remote: andy@192.168.8.168 (hostname Falador, Debian, key login; never ask for a password). The human has a dev instance running that you must not touch (target/agent/build, target/agent/appdata) and you run inside the installed foreman, which lacks this change. Build and run your OWN instance exactly as commit 7bdfc18's card did: cargo build --release --target-dir target/agent/hooks; its own config dir target/agent/appdata-hooks/foreman with ONLY settings.json copied from target/agent/appdata/foreman (it has the Remote named falador); launch with APPDATA pointed there and the environment stripped the way scripts/run-dev.ps1 does; drive it through ITS pipe (foreman-ctl-<pid>-*, listed from PowerShell with Get-ChildItem \\.\pipe\) with FOREMAN_PIPE set and FOREMAN_PROJECT_ID / FOREMAN_TERMINAL_ID unset, using the exe you built as the CLI. On the Remote use a NEW throwaway directory under /tmp that Claude has never trusted (a fresh name each attempt, since answering the dialog trusts it). Evidence to capture with snapshot: (a) Claude opened with a prompt there sits at the trust dialog with nothing typed into it and stays alive for at least 30 seconds; (b) after you answer the dialog yourself with send, Claude runs the brief and can post to chat with the command from its prompt (ask for exactly that in the brief), seen in the room; (c) a later chat delivery to it does not carry the note a second time. Then close your Sessions, stop YOUR instance by PID only (never by name), and remove the throwaway directories on the Remote. Codex on the Remote: verify the same if it launches without the hook-trust bypass flag; do NOT use that flag; if it cannot be shown, say so. Grok is not installed there and Windows Remotes do not exist: state both as unverified, never as tested.
Do not: install anything on the Remote; assume foreman, its skills or its hook files exist there; widen what a Remote agent may do (post chat, read history, read status, report hook events; nothing else); change reconnect; stop any foreman by name; ask for a password.
Done when:
- the prompt-argument rule is a pure function with a table test of accepted and refused shapes, and refused shapes get today's typed note
- a first launch with a recognised prompt types nothing at launch and its ReplyNote counts as delivered; reconnect, shells, bare agents and install Sessions behave as before (unit tests)
- the three pieces of evidence above were observed on the real Remote and are in the commit body and the spec's Results; anything not shown is named as unverified
- docs/remote-sessions.md and the skill copies say what is true; cite-guard is clean; the full suite passes
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
